name: Gradiant 5G Images
what_it_is: A collection of Dockerfiles and Docker Compose deployment examples for Cloud-Native Network Functions (CNFs) targeting 5G (and 4G/EPC) networks, maintained by Gradiant for its Lab5G platform. It provides pre-built container images for two complete 5G core stacks (Open5GS and free5GC) plus simulated RAN/UE components (UERANSIM, PacketRusher, srsRAN) that can be composed into end-to-end 5G testbeds.
components: open5gs (AMF, SMF, UPF, NRF, AUSF, UDM, UDR, PCF, BSF, NSSF, SCP)
free5GC (AMF, SMF, UPF, NRF, AUSF, UDM, UDR, PCF, NSSF)
UERANSIM UE (simulated 5G user equipment, supports multiple UEs per container)
PacketRusher (simulated gNB + UE, HP open-source tool)
protocols: GTP-U tunneling (upf privileged mode, /dev/ogstun tun device)
measurement: End-to-end UE connectivity verified via ping and traceroute over uesimtun0 interface
Throughput testing via iperf3 through UE VRF (ip vrf exec vrf<IMSI> iperf3 -c <server>)
Multiple simultaneous UE tunnels observable as separate tun interfaces (uesimtun0, uesimtun1, …)
configuration: MCC/MNC set via environment variables (MCC, MNC); defaults 999/70
TAC configured via TAC env var on gNB container
Slice selection via SST and SD env vars (default SST=1, SD=0xffffff)
UE credentials via KEY, OP_TYPE (OPC/OP), OP env vars
APN/DNN configured via APN env var on UE container
AMF address resolved by AMF_HOSTNAME env var (DNS lookup inside Docker network)
gNB address resolved by GNB_HOSTNAME env var
N2/N3/RADIO bind IPs configurable via N2_BIND_IP, N3_BIND_IP, RADIO_BIND_IP or derived from named interfaces (N2_IFACE, N3_IFACE, RADIO_IFACE)
SMF config overridden by mounting custom smf.yaml volume
DB_URI env var controls MongoDB connection for PCF, SCP, UDR, WebUI
Multi-UE count set via -n flag on ueransim ue command
NSSF and AMF yaml overrides required for multi-slice deployments
NAT on UPF can be disabled via ENABLE_NAT=false env var (commented out by default)
fault_injection: No dedicated fault injection tooling present in the repository
Individual NF containers can be stopped/restarted independently (restart: on-failure policy) to simulate NF outages
PacketRusher and UERANSIM UE deregistration on SIGTERM can simulate UE detach events
modes: PacketRusher mode (1 simulated gNB + 1 UE, VRF-based isolation)
Open5GS with OAI gNB + USRP hardware (open5gs-and-oai-gnb-usrp)
constraints: UPF container must run privileged (privileged: true, cap_add: all) and requires access to /dev/ogstun tun device on the host
PacketRusher requires Ubuntu 20.04 host with gtp5g kernel module installed and privileged container mode
USRP-based deployments (OAI, srsRAN with hardware) require physical Ettus USRP hardware attached to host
Subscriber registration is a manual prerequisite step (register_subscriber.sh or populate container) before UEs can attach
free5GC deployment uses docker-compose v2.4 (legacy syntax); Open5GS uses v3
Multi-slice operation requires manual override of NSSF and AMF YAML configuration files via volume mounts
notable_absences: No automated subscriber provisioning (registration is a manual shell script step)
No traffic shaping or network emulation (tc/netem) for degraded-link testing
No pre-built test suite or CI pipeline for end-to-end validation
UERANSIM image has no dedicated README (only Dockerfile and entrypoint)
